subject: Staging cutover: asymmetric return-path causing SYN fragmentation and SG drops
messages:
From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@rivermed.com>

Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Rivermed] Post-cutover traffic failures to on-prem DB cluster

Hi Grace,

We completed the staging cutover for private-connect earlier this morning. After the cutover a subset of application servers in AWS can no longer reliably reach our on-premise DB cluster — long TCP handshakes, intermittent resets, and some connections hang after a burst of traffic. We ran a quick traceroute and attached it (rivermed_traceroute_20280914.txt).

Scope: ~4 app hosts showing the same symptoms, ~20% packet loss during initial handshake, and occasional 0-byte TCP acks in captures.

Can Redwood take a look? We believe the private VPC path was in use during the change, but maybe return traffic is taking a different path.

Attachments: rivermed_traceroute_20280914.txt

Thanks,
Alex Morales

Alex / team — I took a look at the traceroute and ran a quick path simulation against our edge maps. The traceroute shows the forward path from the app host to the on‑prem IP traversing our private VPC link, but the return path appears to egress from a different colo-peering (public transit) — that's classical asymmetric return.

Notes:
- Asymmetric return will break TCP when middleboxes (firewalls/NAT) expect symmetric flows.
- The traceroute shows an MTU of ~1400 on one hop (ICMP PMTU tests failing beyond that hop). If MSS isn't clamped, large SYN options or TLS SNI extensions could lead to fragments and retransmits; some middleboxes drop fragments during handshake.
- We see evidence of SNAT on the return path; conntrack state may be created on the public-facing NAT device, and when the SYN/ACK goes back over a different path it doesn't match the expected state.

Immediate suggestions to test (non-invasive):
1) Ask Rivermed to apply a temporary TCP MSS clamp (1300) on the on-prem firewall for the DB subnet and re-test.
2) Collect a pcap at both sides (we need the SYN, SYN/ACK, and any intermediate RSTs).
3) Verify that route advertisements from the private link are preferred (BGP local-pref) — we suspect route prep or MED changes during the cutover.

I can push a routing preference change on our side if you confirm you prefer the private link as active path for that prefix.

– Marissa
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com

Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 10:21:03 -0700
Subject: Re: [Rivermed] Post-cutover traffic failures to on-prem DB cluster

Following up with some kernel/conntrack notes and a short remediation play:

What I pulled from a nearby edge box (attached: edge_conntrack_snapshot.txt):
- High conntrack churn correlated with bursts. Many half-open states (SYN_RECV) time out after ~60s.
- NAT device shows ephemeral port mapping skew when flows egress via public transit — the mapping exists on the public NAT but inbound returns over private link are dropped.

Proposed short-term mitigation (apply in this order):
1) Apply a TCP MSS clamp 1300 on the edge device and ask Rivermed to mirror on their on-prem firewall (low risk).
2) Temporarily relax security group egress/ingress ephemeral port rules for the app and DB subnets to ensure ports 32768–61000 are allowed for short-term testing.
3) If symptoms persist, we perform a BGP tweak: raise local-pref on the private-link-facing neighbors so the return path uses the private link. We'll schedule this for a low-impact window.

Request to Rivermed: upload the pcap capture from their firewall (please include the timestamps). If you can share sample app host IPs we can hit from our test rig.

– Karthik
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@rivermed.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:44:18 -0700
Subject: Re: [Rivermed] Post-cutover traffic failures to on-prem DB cluster

Thanks — attached is a short pcap captured at the on‑prem firewall during a failed handshake (rivermed_staging_pcap_part1.pcap). We tried the MSS clamp on the firewall to 1300 and saw reduced retransmits for a handful of flows, but after a 10–15 minute burst the DB sessions start dropping again.

We also found the on-prem NAT is symmetric and will only accept inbound mappings for connections that originated via the same egress IP. If return traffic uses the public transit NAT, the on-prem device drops the packets.

We can temporarily open ephemeral ports and coordinate a BGP preference change if Redwood is comfortable doing that during a maintenance window.

Attachments: rivermed_staging_pcap_part1.pcap

– Alex
